feedback.problem:
A triangle $D$ has vertices $(-2,-1),(3,-1),(1,3).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992537/assets/10c831c616279f443d10ed478a8b3b173d598da6e9b0b45edb7ecf487cf97f92.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 4=10.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=2\cdot 3-1\cdot 0=6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,6\,|\cdot 10 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
